answer: Rotating Entropy Challenge. Each identity must periodically submit fresh randomness whose statistical fingerprint is checked against a shared marble of prior submissions. Repeats or low-diversity streams reveal clustering like a tide of clones pulling from one source. The check passes only if the stream diverges under a prism test separating independent generators from copied ones. An attacker pays per-identity compute and storage to keep streams distinct, and every detected correlation forfeits that identity's accumulated history.
